summary: The reader has finished an undergraduate computer science degree: asymptotic analysis including recurrences and logarithms, basic discrete mathematics (modular arithmetic, binary representation, divisibility and primes), linear algebra (vectors, matrices, tensor-like indexing of arrays), and elementary algorithms such as schoolbook multiplication. They know Turing machines and tapes, polynomials and complex numbers, but have not studied fast integer multiplication, the FFT in depth, number-theoretic transforms, finite fields, or abstract algebra beyond basics. Specialist material introduced by the paper is not assumed.

known.name: Binary representation of integers
known.gloss: A nonnegative integer is written as a string of bits with place values powers of two, possibly padded with leading zeros to a fixed length.

known.name: Logarithms and floor/ceiling
known.gloss: Base-2 logarithms and rounding functions used to count bits and levels of recursion.

known.name: Modular arithmetic
known.gloss: Arithmetic of integers where numbers are identified when they differ by a multiple of a modulus.

known.name: Primes and coprimality
known.gloss: Prime numbers and pairs of integers with no common factor other than 1.

known.name: Vectors, matrices and linear maps
known.gloss: Finite-dimensional linear algebra including invertible maps, linear combinations, subspaces and rank.

known.name: Tensor (Kronecker) product and multidimensional arrays
known.gloss: Indexing data by several coordinates and applying a linear map to each coordinate or axis separately.

known.name: Roots of unity
known.gloss: Complex numbers w with w^n = 1, such as e^{2 pi i/n}.

known.name: Schoolbook multiplication and basic divide-and-conquer
known.gloss: The quadratic digit-by-digit multiplication algorithm and the idea of splitting a problem into smaller recursive calls.

known.name: Recurrence relations and geometric sums
known.gloss: Solving running-time recurrences and summing geometric series to bound recursive algorithms.

known.name: Floating and fixed-point numbers and rounding
known.gloss: Finite-precision representation of real numbers and bounding the error of approximations, including the maximum norm of a vector.

known.name: Sorting and permutations
known.gloss: Rearranging items by a permutation, and the bitwise exclusive-or operation on bit strings.

known.name: Asymptotic notation variants
known.gloss: Theta and Omega notation for tight and lower bounds, and worst-case time complexity.

known.name: Finite sets, products and maps
known.gloss: Basic set theory including products of sets, bijections, and integers modulo m as an index set.
